newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rose 2.2 pct to 12.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rose 2.2 pct to 12.6 pct.

text.p: A larger share of term loans pushed up the Croatian average lending rate 2.2 percentage points to 12.6 percent in lively trade on Wednesday.
Total settlements, higher at 49 million kuna ($8.1 million), were overshot by 75 million kuna in supply.
All but 18 million kuna accounted for fresh loans, half of which was call money at a stable rate of 10.5 percent. The rest were term deals ranging between 15 and 17 percent.
Insurers rolled over their old one-week loans at nine percent, while banks extended their two-week deals at 14 percent and one-month money at 15 and 16 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday slightly weaker at 6.1173 aginst the dollar and a little firmer at 3.5738 to the German mark.
-- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.015 Croatian Kuna)
